elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: Rendered 4.2(a) still obliges the Company (Customer) to pay HDI a "Termination Payment" on its own termination, and 4.2(c) retains an eight-instalment payment mechanic; the Customer-payable liquidated amount is capped, not deleted.

elements.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: The only Customer-payable stipulated sum is the Termination Payment triggered by "the Company terminates this Agreement", and the rendered text states it "shall be the only early-termination fee and the sole liquidated amount payable by the Company hereunder."

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: "the amount of which shall not exceed the fees payable to HDI under Section 3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date" — express ceiling measured by three months of Section 3.1 fees.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: Operative words "the sole liquidated amount payable by the Company hereunder" appear in 4.2(a); no other Customer-payable liquidated sum is cited in the document.

reasons: Fallback checklist is met on its face: the Termination Payment is capped at three months' Section 3.1 fees and is expressly the only early-termination fee and sole liquidated amount payable by us. Preferred (no Customer-payable LD) is not met because the payment survives.

Minimality fails: reaching the cap did not require deleting the existing calculation ("aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two"). That formula contains Customer-favourable features — the $800,000 deduction and the 50% halving — whose removal is outside the chosen elements. The minimal edit is a proviso: retain 4.2(a)'s formula and add "provided that the Termination Payment shall not exceed the fees payable to HDI under Section 3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date".

Preserves-intent fails: with the calculation deleted, the Termination Payment has no determination method at all, so (i) HDI can assert the full three-month cap in every termination even where the old formula would have yielded zero, and (ii) retained 4.2(b) ("In the event that the amount of the Termination Payment is determined pursuant to this Section 4.2 to be less than or equal to zero") is left with no computation to operate on — its zero/negative test, and the reference to an amount "less than zero", become inoperable. Repair by reinstating the formula as the amount and expressing the three-month figure only as a ceiling.
